"PROJECT: ELDORIA — AGE OF RUIN

Complete Isometric Action RPG

Create an original, exceptionally polished dark fantasy action RPG set in the enormous fantasy world of Eldoria.

The game should take inspiration from the gameplay depth, combat responsiveness, loot systems, character progression, dungeon design, and atmospheric worldbuilding of Diablo IV.

Do not copy Diablo's characters, assets, maps, names, storylines, or interface. Create an entirely original intellectual property.

The objective is to create a deep, replayable action RPG that feels like a professionally developed commercial game.

1. THE WORLD OF ELDORIA

Eldoria was once a prosperous kingdom protected by seven ancient kingdoms and their sacred guardians.

An event known as The Sundering shattered the ancient seals that protected the world.

Now the land is infected by an ancient corruption called The Blight.

Entire cities have fallen. Ancient gods have disappeared. Demons, corrupted beasts, undead armies, and forgotten horrors roam the countryside.

The player is a newly awakened warrior who possesses an unusual ability to absorb fragments of ancient power.

A mysterious voice begins guiding the player, but its true identity and intentions remain unknown.

Create a serious, atmospheric dark fantasy storyline with meaningful characters, memorable villains, cinematic dialogue, major plot twists, and a compelling endgame mystery.

2. GRAPHICAL STYLE

Create a beautiful, dark, highly detailed 2.5D isometric world.

Visual quality is extremely important.

Use:

- Detailed environmental artwork.
- Atmospheric fog and volumetric lighting.
- Dynamic shadows.
- Beautiful spell effects.
- Detailed armor and weapons.
- Smooth character animations.
- Elaborate monster designs.
- Destructible environmental objects where appropriate.
- Detailed dungeon architecture.
- Dynamic weather and lighting.

The world should feel enormous, dangerous, and alive.

Avoid simplistic graphics, placeholder environments, generic assets, and repetitive dungeon rooms.

Maintain a consistent visual art direction throughout the entire game.

3. CAMERA AND MOVEMENT

Use a Diablo-style isometric camera.

Implement:

- Eight-direction movement.
- Smooth character movement.
- Responsive attack animations.
- Camera tracking.
- Mouse and keyboard support.
- Mobile touchscreen controls.
- Zoom controls where appropriate.

The camera must provide a clear view of enemies, attacks, environmental obstacles, and loot.

Combat must feel responsive and satisfying.

4. PLAYABLE CLASSES

Create six distinct playable classes.

WARRIOR:
Heavy armor, swords, axes, shields, powerful physical attacks, and devastating melee abilities.

MAGE:
Elemental magic, lightning, fire, ice, arcane projectiles, and powerful area attacks.

RANGER:
Bows, crossbows, traps, precision attacks, and rapid movement.

NECROMANCER:
Summon undead minions, manipulate souls, curse enemies, and control dark magic.

PALADIN:
Holy abilities, defensive auras, healing, shields, and powerful holy attacks.

ASSASSIN:
Dual blades, stealth, poison, critical strikes, and rapid combos.

Each class must have:

- Unique starting equipment.
- Unique skill trees.
- Class-specific abilities.
- Different combat animations.
- Class-specific passive bonuses.
- Multiple viable character builds.

5. COMBAT SYSTEM

Build a real-time action combat system.

Players should fight groups of enemies using basic attacks, active abilities, dodging, and defensive skills.

Include:

- Basic attacks.
- Six customizable ability slots.
- Cooldowns.
- Mana or class-specific resource management.
- Critical hits.
- Damage numbers.
- Status effects.
- Stuns and knockbacks.
- Area-of-effect attacks.
- Enemy attack indicators.
- Boss mechanics.
- Loot drops.

Combat should become increasingly exciting as players acquire stronger equipment and unlock abilities.

Avoid making enemies passive damage sponges.

Enemies must have recognizable attack patterns, different movement behaviors, and varying difficulty.

6. CHARACTER PROGRESSION

Create a deep progression system.

Include:

- Character levels.
- Attribute points.
- Skill trees.
- Passive abilities.
- Equipment progression.
- Class specialization.
- Legendary powers.
- Set bonuses.
- Endgame progression.

Every level should provide a meaningful improvement or unlock.

Allow players to experiment with different builds.

Make early progression approachable while allowing extremely complex builds at higher levels.

7. LOOT AND EQUIPMENT

Build a comprehensive randomized loot system.

Equipment slots:

- Helmet.
- Chest armor.
- Gloves.
- Pants.
- Boots.
- Main-hand weapon.
- Off-hand item.
- Amulet.
- Two rings.

Loot rarities:

1. Common
2. Magic
3. Rare
4. Epic
5. Legendary
6. Mythic

Equipment must have randomized attributes and meaningful differences.

Legendary items should have unique powers that can fundamentally change how abilities work.

Examples:

- A lightning spell that chains between additional enemies.
- A sword that creates an explosion after consecutive critical hits.
- Armor that summons a protective spirit when health becomes low.
- A bow that splits projectiles into multiple arrows.

Create hundreds of potential equipment combinations as the game expands.

Make loot exciting without making every drop powerful.

8. THE WORLD MAP

Build a large interconnected world containing distinct regions.

THE KINGDOM OF ASH:
Ruined villages, burned castles, undead armies, and abandoned fortresses.

THE WHISPERING WOODS:
Corrupted forests, giant beasts, ancient druid ruins, and hidden shrines.

THE FROZEN CITADEL:
Snow-covered fortresses, frozen caverns, and powerful ice creatures.

THE BLOODLANDS:
A corrupted wasteland filled with demons, blood cults, and dangerous dungeons.

THE SUNKEN KINGDOM:
An ancient civilization buried beneath the earth, containing forgotten treasures and terrifying creatures.

THE SHATTERED THRONE:
An endgame region containing the source of the Blight.

Each region must contain:

- Unique enemies.
- Rare resources.
- Side quests.
- Hidden locations.
- Dungeons.
- Elite monsters.
- World events.
- Region-specific bosses.

9. DUNGEON GENERATION

Create a replayable dungeon system.

Dungeons should feature:

- Randomized room layouts.
- Different enemy combinations.
- Elite enemies.
- Treasure rooms.
- Hidden passages.
- Environmental traps.
- Dungeon objectives.
- Final boss encounters.

Create handcrafted special dungeons with unique storylines and mechanics.

Dungeon difficulty should scale through multiple tiers.

10. ENEMY AND BOSS SYSTEM

Create a large enemy ecosystem.

Enemy categories:

- Undead.
- Demons.
- Corrupted wildlife.
- Cultists.
- Fallen knights.
- Ancient guardians.
- Elemental creatures.
- Eldritch horrors.

Include normal enemies, elite enemies, champions, mini-bosses, and major bosses.

Bosses must have multiple attack patterns, recognizable telegraphs, different combat phases, and unique rewards.

Boss encounters should feel like major accomplishments.

11. QUESTS AND STORY

Create a substantial main campaign with:

- Cinematic opening.
- Fully developed main characters.
- Voice-ready dialogue.
- Side quests.
- Optional discoveries.
- Hidden lore.
- Major story decisions.
- Dramatic boss encounters.
- Multiple story revelations.

The story should unfold naturally through exploration, dialogue, environmental storytelling, and dungeon discoveries.

12. ENDGAME

The game must have meaningful reasons to continue playing after the main campaign.

Include:

- Nightmare dungeon tiers.
- Endgame boss encounters.
- Rare Mythic equipment.
- Legendary crafting.
- Endless challenge dungeons.
- World boss events.
- Class-specific challenges.
- High-difficulty enemy modifiers.
- Build optimization.

The endgame should reward experimentation and mastery rather than simply increasing enemy health indefinitely.

13. USER INTERFACE

Create a premium dark fantasy interface.

Include:

- Character screen.
- Inventory.
- Skill tree.
- World map.
- Quest journal.
- Equipment comparison.
- Loot notifications.
- Settings.
- Main menu.
- Pause menu.

Use detailed icons, elegant typography, dark stone textures, subtle gold accents, and smooth transitions.

The interface must be readable and usable on both desktop and mobile.

14. TECHNICAL REQUIREMENTS

Build a modular, scalable architecture.

Separate the systems for:

- Player movement.
- Combat.
- Classes.
- Skills.
- Enemies.
- Bosses.
- Loot generation.
- Inventory.
- Equipment.
- World generation.
- Dungeon generation.
- Quests.
- Character progression.
- Saving and loading.

Use persistent save data.

Optimize performance for mobile devices and desktop browsers.

Prevent duplicated items, broken inventory states, combat exploits, and lost progression.

15. DEVELOPMENT PRIORITIES

Do not attempt to implement every feature simultaneously.

First create a fully playable vertical slice containing:

1. Main menu.
2. Character selection with all six classes represented.
3. One playable class.
4. A beautiful opening region.
5. Isometric camera and movement.
6. Basic combat.
7. Three enemy types.
8. One elite enemy.
9. One fully functional boss.
10. Basic loot drops.
11. Inventory and equipment.
12. Character leveling.
13. Saving and loading.

Make this first playable area exceptionally polished.

Do not create decorative buttons that do nothing.

Do not replace functional systems with visual mockups.

Preserve existing working systems when expanding the game.

The ultimate goal is a complete, polished, content-rich dark fantasy action RPG set in Eldoria.

---
This is a build request. Build a complete, playable game now (or apply the requested change to the existing game). Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when you finish.

Screenshots for your own checks: save small JPEGs (a .jpg path, viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest one; older images are dropped from context. Read a full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.
"

Empty project. Need to build a complete isometric ARPG. Big task. I have a lot of work. Let me plan architecture.

Given no build tooling, simplest robust approach: vanilla JS ES modules + HTML/CSS, served by a simple static server. Canvas 2D rendering with procedural art (no external assets). Could use Three.js for 3D isometric? The requirement says 2.5D isometric with high visual quality. Canvas 2D with rich procedural rendering can look very good and is reliable. Alternatively use Three.js via CDN — but offline? Need reliable capture in browser. Using CDN may fail. We could install three via npm and bundle? Simpler: Canvas 2D with careful rendering: terrain tiles, fog gradients, shadows, particles, spell effects. That can be polished.

I should build a substantial game:

- Main menu with title, New Game / Continue / Settings / Credits.
- Character creation with 6 classes represented, selectable all 6 (not just one — better).
- Isometric world, camera, 8-direction movement WASD, click-to-move maybe.
- Combat: basic attack, 6 abilities with cooldowns, resource, dodge, damage numbers, status effects, crits, telegraphs.
- Enemies: 3+ types, elite, boss with phases.
- Loot: 10 slots, 6 rarities, affixes, legendaries with powers, pickups, inventory/equipment UI, comparison tooltip.
- Progression: levels, XP, attributes, skill tree (per class), passives.
- Quests: main campaign with dialogue, side quests, journal.
- Regions: 6 regions on world map, travel between them; at least one fully polished opening region + others playable with scaling.
- Dungeons: procedural rooms, objectives, boss, tiers (rift).
- Endgame: nightmare tiers, endless challenge.
- Save/load localStorage.
- UI: premium dark fantasy, responsive, mobile touch joystick + buttons.
- Audio: procedural WebAudio (ambient, hits, spells) — adds a lot of polish. Optional mute.
- Performance: efficient canvas.

This is huge but doable if I write a well-organized set of ES modules. Let me estimate code: maybe 6000-9000 lines. I need to be efficient. I'll write in chunks.

Let me decide rendering approach more concretely. A top-down/isometric canvas renderer:

World coordinates (x,y) on ground plane. Screen: sx = (x-y)*cos(30°)... Standard isometric: screenX = (x - y) * tileW/2, screenY = (x + y) * tileH/2. But movement in world grid. Terrain: generate a heightless tile map with tiles ~ 64x32. Draw with per-tile art variations. Alternatively use a "2.5D" projection where characters are billboard sprites drawn with vertical offset and shadow. Entities drawn as procedural layered shapes (armor, cloaks) with animation. That can look decent if detailed.

I could go 3D with Three.js for much better visuals: actual isometric camera, lighting, fog, shadows, instanced terrain, 3D characters built from primitives, particles. That could look dramatically better than flat canvas. But complexity of animation and assets is high, and performance in SwiftShader capture may be poor. However the environment mentions WebGPU capture and Three.js. Hmm, capture uses SwiftShader CPU — 3D could be slow but a simple scene is fine.

Risk assessment: Canvas 2D gives full control, guaranteed screenshot output, easier UI overlays, and can look quite atmospheric with gradients, glow, particles, fog layers, lighting. I'm confident in producing a polished 2D isometric look. I'll go with Canvas 2D + procedural art, high DPI, layered parallax, dynamic lighting via composite operations.

Let me design the code structure:

```
index.html
styles.css
src/main.js

```

Maybe simpler to have fewer large modules but modular separation as required. Let's aim ~12 modules.

Core game design details:

World: each region is a large map (e.g., 160x160 tiles at 1 unit). Tile-based terrain with props. Player moves continuously. Camera follows. Enemies wander/chase. Points of interest: dungeons entrances, NPCs, shrines, chests.

Map generation: deterministic seeded. Regions handcrafted via generation parameters: biome palettes, props, enemy sets, boss. The opening region "The Kingdom of Ash" with a ruined village, ash fields, a road, graveyard, fortress dungeon. Generate with noise + hand-placed features. To look polished, render terrain with layered textures: base color, noise speckles, cracks, grass tufts, stones; fog vignette; light pools. Draw order sorted by y.

Rendering entities: characters as procedural vector shapes with skeletal-ish animation. Need classes visually distinct: warrior with sword/shield and cape; mage robe/staff; ranger hood/bow; necromancer dark robe/skull staff; paladin plate/hammer/halo; assassin dual daggers/hood. Draw with shapes and gradients, animated limbs based on time and state (walk cycle, attack swing).

Enemies: undead (skeletal), demon (horned), corrupted beast (wolf), cultist, knight, guardian, elemental, horror. Draw similarly procedural.

Boss: big unique shape with phases and telegraphs.

FX: slashes, projectiles, explosions, lightning chains, frost novas, poison clouds, blood, sparks, floating damage numbers, loot beams, screen shake, hit flash, ground decals (telegraph circles).

UI: HTML/CSS overlay panels (inventory, skills, map, journal, settings), with gold/dark stone aesthetic. Use custom fonts via system serif stacks (no network). Maybe embed Google Fonts? No network guarantee. Use "Cinzel"? Not available. Use Georgia/Trajan-like? System fonts: 'Palatino Linotype', 'Book Antiqua', Georgia, serif for headers. Letter-spacing uppercase gives premium feel. Could fetch fonts from Google — risky offline. Stick to system.

HUD: health globe (left), resource globe (right), ability bar with 6 slots and cooldown radial, XP bar, minimap, quest tracker, region name, level, gold. Diablo-style orbs are iconic but need original: use ornate soul lanterns / runic vessels. I'll do ornate angular orbs.

- Leveling: XP curve, +1 attribute point per level, +1 skill point; skill tree with nodes.

- Dungeons: generated rooms connected by corridors on a grid; enemies spawn; objective (slay X, destroy seals, find relic); boss room; exit portal; tiers.
- Quests: main story chain across regions with dialogue popups; side quests per region; journal; rewards. NPC dialogue with portraits (procedural faces? maybe sigil icons).
- World map overlay: clickable regions with level ranges, unlock progression.
- Endgame: Nightmare tiers from dungeon completion, "Abyssal Rift" endless waves, world boss events in regions, mythic drops.

Save/load: JSON to localStorage, autosave on region change/level up, versioned.

Mobile: virtual joystick, ability buttons, responsive UI.

Audio: WebAudio synth for ambience + sfx. Keep subtle, toggle.

I need to be pragmatic: implement deep enough systems and ensure no dead buttons. All menus functional.

Time budget: I'll write code over multiple tool calls. Let's start with scaffolding.

Let me write CSS substantial.

Let me define data carefully.

Classes:
- warrior: resource rage (0-100, builds on hit, decays), primary stat str. Skills: Cleave, Charge, Whirlwind, War Cry, Shield Wall, Earthquake, Bloodthirst, Iron Skin, Executioner, Berserk.
- mage: mana 100. Fireball, Frost Nova, Chain Lightning, Arcane Orb, Meteor, Blink, Ice Armor, Flame Wall, Thunderstorm, Time Warp.
- ranger: focus 100. Piercing Arrow, Multishot, Trap, Roll, Poison Arrow, Rain of Arrows, Hunter's Mark, Volley, Shadowstep, Beast Companion.

Each skill node: id, name, branch, tier, maxRank, requires, type, cost, cooldown, damage multiplier, radius, etc. To simplify implementation, define "effect" descriptors used by combat engine. 10 skills per class ×6 = 60. That's a lot of data but fine.

Maybe 8 skills per class + passives. Requirement: 6 customizable slots. Let's do 12 nodes per class including passives, with ~9 active.

Combat engine: unified ability executor with kinds:
- melee_arc (cone AoE in facing dir)
- projectile (single/multiple, pierce, chain, split)
- nova (radial)
- ground_aoe (targeted at cursor)
- dash (move + damage along path)

- trap (placed, triggers)
- beam/channel maybe skip

Projectiles update with collision.

World gen: For performance, render tiles in viewport only. Tile size world 1 unit; iso projection scale. Number of visible tiles maybe ~ (screen/48) ~ 30x30=900 diamonds each frame plus details — okay.

Props drawn per tile: trees, rocks, ruins, gravestones, braziers, crates (destructible). Need collision: simple circle colliders. Mouse click to move: raycast inverse iso from screen to world; set target. Keyboard WASD moves screen-relative? 8-direction: in iso, W moves up-screen = world (-x,-y). I'll map keys to world axes with iso alignment: W = (-1,-1)/√2, S=(1,1), A=(-1,1), D=(1,-1). Good.

2. "The Silent Bell" — investigate the ruined chapel, kill elite Bell-warden, retrieve Relic.

"PROJECT: ELDORIA — AGE OF RUIN

Complete Isometric Action RPG

Create an original, exceptionally polished dark fantasy action RPG set in the enormous fantasy world of Eldoria.

The game should take inspiration from the gameplay depth, combat responsiveness, loot systems, character progression, dungeon design, and atmospheric worldbuilding of Diablo IV.

Do not copy Diablo's characters, assets, maps, names, storylines, or interface. Create an entirely original intellectual property.

The objective is to create a deep, replayable action RPG that feels like a professionally developed commercial game.

1. THE WORLD OF ELDORIA

Eldoria was once a prosperous kingdom protected by seven ancient kingdoms and their sacred guardians.

An event known as The Sundering shattered the ancient seals that protected the world.

Now the land is infected by an ancient corruption called The Blight.

Entire cities have fallen. Ancient gods have disappeared. Demons, corrupted beasts, undead armies, and forgotten horrors roam the countryside.

The player is a newly awakened warrior who possesses an unusual ability to absorb fragments of ancient power.

A mysterious voice begins guiding the player, but its true identity and intentions remain unknown.

Create a serious, atmospheric dark fantasy storyline with meaningful characters, memorable villains, cinematic dialogue, major plot twists, and a compelling endgame mystery.

2. GRAPHICAL STYLE

Create a beautiful, dark, highly detailed 2.5D isometric world.

Visual quality is extremely important.

Use:

- Detailed environmental artwork.
- Atmospheric fog and volumetric lighting.
- Dynamic shadows.
- Beautiful spell effects.
- Detailed armor and weapons.
- Smooth character animations.
- Elaborate monster designs.
- Destructible environmental objects where appropriate.
- Detailed dungeon architecture.
- Dynamic weather and lighting.

The world should feel enormous, dangerous, and alive.

Avoid simplistic graphics, placeholder environments, generic assets, and repetitive dungeon rooms.

Maintain a consistent visual art direction throughout the entire game.

3. CAMERA AND MOVEMENT

Use a Diablo-style isometric camera.

Implement:

- Eight-direction movement.
- Smooth character movement.
- Responsive attack animations.
- Camera tracking.
- Mouse and keyboard support.
- Mobile touchscreen controls.
- Zoom controls where appropriate.

The camera must provide a clear view of enemies, attacks, environmental obstacles, and loot.

Combat must feel responsive and satisfying.

4. PLAYABLE CLASSES

Create six distinct playable classes.

WARRIOR:
Heavy armor, swords, axes, shields, powerful physical attacks, and devastating melee abilities.

MAGE:
Elemental magic, lightning, fire, ice, arcane projectiles, and powerful area attacks.

RANGER:
Bows, crossbows, traps, precision attacks, and rapid movement.

NECROMANCER:
Summon undead minions, manipulate souls, curse enemies, and control dark magic.

PALADIN:
Holy abilities, defensive auras, healing, shields, and powerful holy attacks.

ASSASSIN:
Dual blades, stealth, poison, critical strikes, and rapid combos.

Each class must have:

- Unique starting equipment.
- Unique skill trees.
- Class-specific abilities.
- Different combat animations.
- Class-specific passive bonuses.
- Multiple viable character builds.

5. COMBAT SYSTEM

Build a real-time action combat system.

Players should fight groups of enemies using basic attacks, active abilities, dodging, and defensive skills.

Include:

- Basic attacks.
- Six customizable ability slots.
- Cooldowns.
- Mana or class-specific resource management.
- Critical hits.
- Damage numbers.
- Status effects.
- Stuns and knockbacks.
- Area-of-effect attacks.
- Enemy attack indicators.
- Boss mechanics.
- Loot drops.

Combat should become increasingly exciting as players acquire stronger equipment and unlock abilities.

Avoid making enemies passive damage sponges.

Enemies must have recognizable attack patterns, different movement behaviors, and varying difficulty.

6. CHARACTER PROGRESSION

Create a deep progression system.

Include:

- Character levels.
- Attribute points.
- Skill trees.
- Passive abilities.
- Equipment progression.
- Class specialization.
- Legendary powers.
- Set bonuses.
- Endgame progression.

Every level should provide a meaningful improvement or unlock.

Allow players to experiment with different builds.

Make early progression approachable while allowing extremely complex builds at higher levels.

7. LOOT AND EQUIPMENT

Build a comprehensive randomized loot system.

Equipment slots:

- Helmet.
- Chest armor.
- Gloves.
- Pants.
- Boots.
- Main-hand weapon.
- Off-hand item.
- Amulet.
- Two rings.

Loot rarities:

1. Common
2. Magic
3. Rare
4. Epic
5. Legendary
6. Mythic

Equipment must have randomized attributes and meaningful differences.

Legendary items should have unique powers that can fundamentally change how abilities work.

Examples:

- A lightning spell that chains between additional enemies.
- A sword that creates an explosion after consecutive critical hits.
- Armor that summons a protective spirit when health becomes low.
- A bow that splits projectiles into multiple arrows.

Create hundreds of potential equipment combinations as the game expands.

Make loot exciting without making every drop powerful.

8. THE WORLD MAP

Build a large interconnected world containing distinct regions.

THE KINGDOM OF ASH:
Ruined villages, burned castles, undead armies, and abandoned fortresses.

THE WHISPERING WOODS:
Corrupted forests, giant beasts, ancient druid ruins, and hidden shrines.

THE FROZEN CITADEL:
Snow-covered fortresses, frozen caverns, and powerful ice creatures.

THE BLOODLANDS:
A corrupted wasteland filled with demons, blood cults, and dangerous dungeons.

THE SUNKEN KINGDOM:
An ancient civilization buried beneath the earth, containing forgotten treasures and terrifying creatures.

THE SHATTERED THRONE:
An endgame region containing the source of the Blight.

Each region must contain:

- Unique enemies.
- Rare resources.
- Side quests.
- Hidden locations.
- Dungeons.
- Elite monsters.
- World events.
- Region-specific bosses.

9. DUNGEON GENERATION

Create a replayable dungeon system.

Dungeons should feature:

- Randomized room layouts.
- Different enemy combinations.
- Elite enemies.
- Treasure rooms.
- Hidden passages.
- Environmental traps.
- Dungeon objectives.
- Final boss encounters.

Create handcrafted special dungeons with unique storylines and mechanics.

Dungeon difficulty should scale through multiple tiers.

10. ENEMY AND BOSS SYSTEM

Create a large enemy ecosystem.

Enemy categories:

- Undead.
- Demons.
- Corrupted wildlife.
- Cultists.
- Fallen knights.
- Ancient guardians.
- Elemental creatures.
- Eldritch horrors.

Include normal enemies, elite enemies, champions, mini-bosses, and major bosses.

Bosses must have multiple attack patterns, recognizable telegraphs, different combat phases, and unique rewards.

Boss encounters should feel like major accomplishments.

11. QUESTS AND STORY

Create a substantial main campaign with:

- Cinematic opening.
- Fully developed main characters.
- Voice-ready dialogue.
- Side quests.
- Optional discoveries.
- Hidden lore.
- Major story decisions.
- Dramatic boss encounters.
- Multiple story revelations.

The story should unfold naturally through exploration, dialogue, environmental storytelling, and dungeon discoveries.

12. ENDGAME

The game must have meaningful reasons to continue playing after the main campaign.

Include:

- Nightmare dungeon tiers.
- Endgame boss encounters.
- Rare Mythic equipment.
- Legendary crafting.
- Endless challenge dungeons.
- World boss events.
- Class-specific challenges.
- High-difficulty enemy modifiers.
- Build optimization.

The endgame should reward experimentation and mastery rather than simply increasing enemy health indefinitely.

13. USER INTERFACE

Create a premium dark fantasy interface.

Include:

- Character screen.
- Inventory.
- Skill tree.
- World map.
- Quest journal.
- Equipment comparison.
- Loot notifications.
- Settings.
- Main menu.
- Pause menu.

Use detailed icons, elegant typography, dark stone textures, subtle gold accents, and smooth transitions.

The interface must be readable and usable on both desktop and mobile.

14. TECHNICAL REQUIREMENTS

Build a modular, scalable architecture.

Separate the systems for:

- Player movement.
- Combat.
- Classes.
- Skills.
- Enemies.
- Bosses.
- Loot generation.
- Inventory.
- Equipment.
- World generation.
- Dungeon generation.
- Quests.
- Character progression.
- Saving and loading.

Use persistent save data.

Optimize performance for mobile devices and desktop browsers.

Prevent duplicated items, broken inventory states, combat exploits, and lost progression.

15. DEVELOPMENT PRIORITIES

Do not attempt to implement every feature simultaneously.

First create a fully playable vertical slice containing:

1. Main menu.
2. Character selection with all six classes represented.
3. One playable class.
4. A beautiful opening region.
5. Isometric camera and movement.
6. Basic combat.
7. Three enemy types.
8. One elite enemy.
9. One fully functional boss.
10. Basic loot drops.
11. Inventory and equipment.
12. Character leveling.
13. Saving and loading.

Make this first playable area exceptionally polished.

Do not create decorative buttons that do nothing.

Do not replace functional systems with visual mockups.

Preserve existing working systems when expanding the game.

The ultimate goal is a complete, polished, content-rich dark fantasy action RPG set in Eldoria.

---

Screenshots for your own checks: save small JPEGs (a .jpg path, viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest one; older images are dropped from context. Read a full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.
